concepts: how the client calls the server
flow:
Pattern — DDP Method Dispatch:
Client calls sdk.call('methodName') → DDP protocol over WebSocket → server Meteor.methods({ methodName }) handles it.
The indexer connects client and server via shared method names: graph("methodName", "up") shows client caller, graph("methodName", "down") shows server handler.
If you see sdk.call('X') on client side, search("X", layer="server") to find the server handler.

Pattern — Callback Event System:
callbacks.run('eventName') executes all registered handlers sequentially → callbacks.add('eventName', handler, priority) registers listeners sorted by priority.
These are NOT connected by imports. Use graph("eventName", "down", edgeTypes=["event_listen"]) to find all registered handlers.
Common events: afterSaveMessage (notifications, autotranslate, slackbridge, apps engine), afterSaveUser, afterDeleteMessage, afterCreateChannel.

Pattern — core-services Bus:
Services do NOT call each other via direct imports. They use proxify('IServiceName') → api.call('namespace.method') → LocalBroker.call() → bound ServiceClass method.
LocalBroker stores methods as 'serviceName.methodName' → bound function. Services extend ServiceClassInternal (monolith) or ServiceClass.
If graph can't find a service, search for the class name (e.g., search("RoomService")).

concepts: how a message appears live on the client
flow:
Pattern — Real-time Streaming:
After DB write: notifyOnMessageChange() → api.broadcast('watch.messages') → ListenersModule event handler → streamRoomMessage.emitWithoutBroadcast(roomId, message) → Streamer._emit() → DDP WebSocket → client Streamer.receive().
Client subscribes via Meteor.subscribe() or Streamer.on(). StreamerCentral is the singleton managing all streamer instances.
Authorization: streamRoomMessage.allowRead() checks canReadRoom() before delivering.

Pattern — Apps Engine Hooks:
Apps register lifecycle hooks (IPreMessageSent, IPostMessageSent, etc.) → AppListenerManager.executeListener() fires them.
In sendMessage flow: Apps.triggerEvent(IPreMessageSentPrevent) can block sending, IPreMessageSentModify can alter the message, IPostMessageSent fires after save.
Bridge layer adapts between core RC and App sandbox. The connection is event-based, not import-based.

concepts: how a message is rendered from text to react
flow:
Pattern — Message Rendering Pipeline:
This is a data transformation pipeline, NOT a call chain. graph cannot fully traverse it.
Flow: message.msg → parse() (packages/message-parser) → AST nodes → <Markup> component (packages/gazzodown) → block components (ParagraphBlock, HeadingBlock, QuoteBlock etc.).
Use implement on parse() and Markup separately — they are in different packages.

concepts: sending a message on the client side
how a message is sent from the client
flow:
Architecture — Client Message Flow:
RoomBody renders <RoomComposer> wrapping <ComposerContainer>.
ComposerContainer is a conditional renderer — checks room state (archived, read-only, omnichannel, federated, anonymous, blocked) and renders the appropriate composer variant. For normal rooms → ComposerMessage.
ComposerMessage wires onSend: stops typing indicator → chat.flows.sendMessage({ text, tshow, previewUrls, tmid }).
MessageBox is the actual textarea UI — handleSendMessage gets text from chat.composer, calls onSend prop.
The flow ends with sdk.call('sendMessage') crossing the DDP boundary.

concepts: sending a message on the server side
how a message is validated and saved
flow:
Architecture — Server Message Flow:
Meteor.methods({ sendMessage }) validates user → calls executeSendMessage(uid, message).
executeSendMessage: validates thread params, checks timestamp within 60s, validates message size, then calls canSendMessageAsync(rid, user) for room access/permission checks.
canSendMessageAsync → validateRoomMessagePermissionsAsync: checks room exists, not archived, canAccessRoom, not blocked, read-only permissions, muted status.
Then calls sendMessage(user, message, room): validateMessage (XSS in hrefs, attachments, custom fields) → prepareMessageObject → Apps Engine pre-hooks (IPreMessageSentPrevent/Modify) → Message.beforeSave → Messages.insertOne → Apps Engine post-hooks → afterSaveMessage → notifyOnRoomChangedById.

Architecture — Notifications:
Triggered by afterSaveMessage callback (registered with LOW priority).
sendAllNotifications → sendMessageNotifications → per-user sendNotification which checks:
- shouldNotifyDesktop → notifyDesktopUser() (sent immediately, NOT queued)
- shouldNotifyMobile → Notification.scheduleItem({type:'push'}) (queued with delay: 120s online, 0s offline)
- shouldNotifyEmail → Notification.scheduleItem({type:'email'}) (queued)
NotificationQueue worker processes queue: push items → PushNotification.send() → PushClass.
PushClass routing: if gateway mode → HTTP POST to cloud gateway; if native mode → sendAPN() for Apple / sendFCM() for Google Firebase.
Can be disabled via Troubleshoot_Disable_Notifications setting.

concepts: how endpoints are registered in the rest api
flow:
Architecture — REST API:
API.v1 is created via createApi({ version:'v1', useDefaultAuth:true }). Routes registered via APIClass.addRoute() (legacy) or typed .get()/.post()/.put()/.delete() methods.
Full middleware chain: WebApp.rawConnectHandlers → remoteAddressMiddleware → CORS → logger → metrics → tracerSpan → router dispatch → authenticationMiddlewareForHono → permissionsMiddleware → license check → route handler.
authenticationMiddleware validates x-user-id + x-auth-token headers or OAuth tokens.
Route handlers receive APIActionContext with this.bodyParams, this.queryParams, this.user, and return API.v1.success()/failure().

concepts: using a model to query data
flow:
Architecture — Database Models:
All models extend BaseRaw<T> which wraps MongoDB collection operations (find, findOne, insertOne, updateOne, deleteOne, etc.).
Pattern: 1) define document interface in core-typings (extends IRocketChatRecord) → 2) define model interface in model-typings (extends IBaseModel<T>) → 3) implement class extending BaseRaw in models package → 4) register via registerModel in server startup.
Models are accessed via proxified imports: e.g., import { Messages } from '@rocket.chat/models' → proxify routes through LocalBroker.
BaseRaw provides modelIndexes() override for MongoDB index definitions.

Architecture — Livechat / Omnichannel:
New conversation: QueueManager.requestRoom() creates room + inquiry in a transaction → processNewInquiry() checks inquiry status: if READY → RoutingManager.delegateInquiry() immediately; if QUEUED → saves to queue.
RoutingManager.delegateInquiry() → routing strategy (AutoSelection, Manual, etc.) → takeInquiry() assigns agent → assignAgent() updates room.
Background queue: OmnichannelService starts OmnichannelQueue worker → execute() loop processes queued inquiries → calls RoutingManager.delegateInquiry().
Room closing: closeRoom() runs in a MongoDB transaction — closes room, removes inquiry, removes subscriptions, then afterRoomClosed() saves system message + triggers app events.

Architecture — Authentication / LDAP:
Login: Meteor.loginWith*() → Accounts.registerLoginHandler dispatches to registered handlers.
LDAP flow: configureLDAP() registers handler with Accounts.registerLoginHandler('ldap', fn) → checks for ldap flag in login request → calls LDAP.loginRequest(username, password) via core-services proxy → LDAPService.loginRequest() → LDAPManager.login().
LDAPManager.login(): creates LDAPConnection → ldap.connect() → ldap.searchByUsername() → ldap.authenticate(dn, password) → checks group filter → finds/creates user in MongoDB → syncs avatar → returns {userId}.
Fallback: if LDAP fails and LDAP_Login_Fallback enabled → Accounts._runLoginHandlers() for default password auth.
beforeValidateLogin callback prevents password logins for LDAP users unless fallback is enabled.

Architecture — Settings:
Settings are registered via SettingsRegistry.add() → stored in MongoDB via Settings model → cached in memory by CachedSettings (Map-based store with Emitter).
Client access: Meteor methods 'public-settings/get' and 'private-settings/get'.
Services watch settings via CachedSettings.watch(settingId, callback) or CachedSettings.watchByRegex(regex, callback). CachedSettings.change() for direct updates.
Search for "SettingsRegistry" to find registration, "CachedSettings" for the cache layer.

Architecture — Enterprise Licensing:
LicenseManager validates license → LicenseImp handles implementation → modules are gated via hasModule() checks throughout the codebase.
License changes emit events via onValidateLicense listeners. Enterprise features check hasModule() before enabling.
Located in ee/packages/license/.

Architecture — Federation:
Outgoing: FederationMatrix.sendMessage() → federationSDK.sendMessage() → Matrix protocol HTTP API to remote server.
Incoming: PUT /_matrix/federation/v1/send/:txnId → federationSDK.processIncomingTransaction() → event emitter dispatches by type → event listeners (e.g., 'homeserver.matrix.message') process and persist to local DB.
Uses event-driven architecture internally, not direct function calls. Located in ee/packages/federation-matrix/.

concepts: what happens when a user creates a channel
create a room or direct message
flow:
Architecture — Room Creation:
DDP method createChannel → createChannelMethod validates params → calls createRoom().
createRoom sequence: prepareCreateRoomCallback.run() → Apps Engine pre-hooks (IPreRoomCreatePrevent/Modify/Extend) → beforeCreateRoomCallback.run() → Rooms.createWithFullRoomData() → createUsersSubscriptions() → callbacks.runAsync('afterCreateChannel'/'afterCreatePrivateGroup'/'afterCreateRoom') → Apps.triggerEvent(IPostRoomCreate).
Direct messages: createDirectMessage → createDirectRoom with type 'd'.
RoomService (via proxify) also exposes create/createDirectMessage.

Architecture — File Upload:
Client: uploadFiles() handles file selection and upload UI.
Server: two-step REST flow: 1) POST rooms.media/:rid uploads file to storage, 2) POST rooms.mediaConfirm/:rid/:fileId confirms upload and creates message with attachment.
FileUploadClass processes files. Storage backends are pluggable: GridFS (default), S3, WebDAV, FileSystem.
File metadata stored in Uploads collection. sendFileMessage() creates the chat message with attachment reference.

Architecture — E2E Encryption:
All client-side in apps/meteor/client/lib/e2ee/.
E2E class: createAndLoadKeys() generates RSA key pair. Private key is encrypted using PBKDF2 key derivation (password → derived key) then AES-GCM encryption (derived key → encrypted private key).
Per-room: E2ERoom.createGroupKey() generates AES session key, encrypts it with each member's RSA public key via encryptGroupKeyForParticipant().
Keychain manages encrypted key storage using EncryptedKeyCodec. crypto/ has rsa.ts, aes.ts, pbkdf2.ts.
Server enforces E2E_Enable and E2E_Allow_Unencrypted_Messages settings.

Architecture — Two-Factor Authentication:
twoFactorRequired() is a middleware wrapper applied to sensitive methods/endpoints.
When triggered: calls checkCodeForUser() which tries verification methods in order: TOTPCheck (authenticator app) → EmailCheck (email code) → PasswordCheckFallback.
Each check implements ICodeCheck interface with verify() and isEnabled() methods.
TOTP uses standard RFC 6238 time-based codes. Email sends a temporary code via Mailer.

concepts: slash command from client to server
flow:
Architecture — Slash Commands:
Client side: in sendMessage flow, processSlashCommand() parses message with regex /^\/([^\s]+)(.*)/ to detect commands.
Client does NOT run commands directly — it calls sdk.call('slashCommand', { cmd, params, msg, triggerId }) which crosses DDP to the server.
Server side: slashCommands registry has add() to register and run() to execute. Built-in commands (invite, kick, join, etc.) register via slashCommands.add().

Architecture — Webhooks / Integrations:
Incoming: POST /hooks/:integrationId/:token → executeIntegrationRest() authenticates → runs integration script in isolated-vm sandbox → processWebhookMessage() creates message from webhook payload.
Outgoing: triggerHandler listens for message events → matches configured triggers → executes outgoing webhook script → sends HTTP request to external URL.
Integration scripts run in isolated-vm for security. History tracked via updateHistory().

Architecture — Message Search:
SearchProviderService manages search providers. DefaultProvider uses MongoDB text search ($text index).
Pluggable: other providers (e.g., Elasticsearch) can be registered.
Client calls search API → SearchProviderService.search() → active provider's search() method → returns results.

Architecture — Teams:
TeamService extends ServiceClassInternal, accessed via proxify pattern.
Teams are a layer above rooms — a team contains multiple channels. TeamService handles create, addMembers, removeMembers, listRooms.
Data stored in Team and TeamMember models (packages/models).

concepts: how the video conference system works
flow:
Architecture — Video Conference:
VideoConfService extends ServiceClassInternal, accessed via proxify pattern.
Providers are pluggable via videoConfProviders registry. Default providers integrate with Jitsi and others via Apps Engine.
Client-side VideoConfManager handles call lifecycle (ring, accept, reject). isRoomCompatibleWithVideoConfRinging checks room eligibility.

concepts: how the auto translate feature works
flow:
Architecture — Auto-Translate:
Registered as afterSaveMessage callback with MEDIUM priority.
TranslationProviderRegistry manages providers: GoogleAutoTranslate, MSTranslate, DeepLTranslate.
When enabled for a room: afterSaveMessage → provider.translateMessage() → stores translations in message.translations field.
Each provider implements AutoTranslate base class with _translateMessage() method.

Architecture — User Presence:
Presence extends ServiceClass (EE package in ee/packages/presence/). Tracks online/away/offline status per connection.
Flow: client calls setUserStatus() method → Presence.setStatus(uid, statusType) → broadcasts status change → StreamPresence delivers to subscribed clients.
PresenceReaper cleans stale connections every 5 minutes (batch of 500). License-gated: unlimited-presence and scalability modules control broadcast behavior.
Custom status: insertOrUpdateUserStatus() / deleteCustomUserStatus() methods.

concepts: how the data import system works
flow:
Architecture — Data Import System:
Plugin architecture: base Importer class → concrete importers (CsvImporter, SlackImporter, SlackUsersImporter, ContactImporter).
ImportersContainer is a registry — importers register via Importers.add(info).
Flow: uploadImportFile() → prepareUsingLocalFile() (parse ZIP) → ImportDataConverter normalizes to RC format → user reviews selection → startImport() processes data.
Progress tracked via ImporterProgress with WebSocket updates to UI. ZIP-based: all import data packaged as ZIP archives.

Architecture — Email System:
Functional module (NOT class-based). Search for "Mailer" or "sendNoWrap" to find it.
Key functions: send() wraps content with header/footer template + CSS inlining via juice, sendNoWrap() sends raw email.
Template system: getTemplate() watches settings for Email_Header/Email_Footer, applies inlinecss() with debouncing.
Variable replacement: replace() and replaceEscaped() for data interpolation.
Apps Engine integration: IPreEmailSent event hook before sending.
Uses Meteor's Email.sendAsync() under the hood.

Architecture — Server Startup & Migrations:
Boot order: main.ts → Promise.all([configureServer(settings), registerServices(), startup()]) → startRocketChat() → startRestAPI().
Migrations: addMigration({ version, name, up() }) registers versioned DB migrations. Framework uses atomic MongoDB lock on migrations.control to prevent concurrent runs.
onServerVersionChange() detects version upgrades for one-time tasks (permission upserts, cloud registration).
Fresh databases (version 0) skip all migrations.
